title: Flo Alternatives in Nigeria: Four Trackers, Compared
description: Compare four Flo alternatives for Nigerian women trying to conceive. See reminders, prices, sign-up and what each tracker lets you do with your dates.
share: If you want an alternative to Flo in Nigeria, this comparison shows what four period trackers let you do, what they cost and where they keep your dates.
kicker: For Nigerian women who want another option beside Flo
answer: If you are trying to conceive and want to see your fertile days without signing up, choose Wholesome Girlies. If you want reminders and years of period dates in one app, choose Period Calendar. If you like reading expert-written guides beside your tracker, choose Clue. If you want one app that stays with you through pregnancy and after the birth, choose Ovia. No app here can tell you the exact day you ovulate from dates alone.

picks.name: Wholesome Girlies
picks.label: Best if you are trying to conceive and want a plan
picks.suits: You want to see your fertile days without signing up, keep your dates on your phone, and go to the clinic with your questions ready.
picks.price: The tools need no card. The Blueprint is one payment of ₦5,700 early-bird (₦13,700 standard), or $12 early-bird ($27 standard) abroad. There is no subscription and nothing to cancel.
can: Type the day your last period started and see your fertile days on the same screen.
Log the first day of each period. After three, it works out your own cycle length.
Tap Add to my calendar to put your next periods and fertile days in your phone calendar, with a reminder 2 days before.
Print a list of questions for your fertility doctor.
Send your husband a checklist of what he can do for his sperm health.
Add the Girlies app to your home screen straight from our page, with no app store download. Once it is added, the tools work even when you have no data.
Keep using it when you get pregnant, after the birth and while you raise your child.

For a full plan, buy The Trying-to-Conceive Blueprint, paid once with no subscription. It explains your cycle, getting your body ready, his part, your tests and the wait, and you join a community of women who are trying too.
cannot: You cannot note symptoms or moods.
It cannot detect ovulation. It counts 14 days back from your next expected period, so we make no accuracy claim.

picks.name: Clue
picks.label: Best if you like reading guides beside your tracker
picks.suits: You want a cycle tracker with expert-written guides, and you do not mind advice that was not written for Nigeria.
picks.price: Clue Plus costs ₦1,500 (about $1) to ₦12,900 (about $10) on the Nigerian App Store.
can: Track your cycle in an app made in Berlin.
Read expert-written guides about your cycle.
Clue says it does not sell your data to advertisers.
cannot: Forecasts of your next dates need Clue Plus, its paid version.
Its guides are not written for Nigeria. It ranks 46 in the Nigerian App Store Health and Fitness chart.

picks.name: Period Calendar
picks.label: Best for reminders and years of history
picks.suits: You want reminders before your period and want to keep years of period dates in one app.
picks.price: Its paid versions cost ₦500 (about $0.40) for 7 days of Premium, up to ₦69,900 (about $52) for Pro, on the Nigerian App Store.
can: Keep years of period dates in one calendar.
It ranks 2 in the Nigerian App Store Health and Fitness chart and first in Nigerian Google Play search for period tracker.
cannot: It shows ads. Google Play marks it as containing ads, and reviews mention ads and upgrade pop-ups.

picks.name: Ovia
picks.label: Best for one app through pregnancy and after the birth
picks.suits: You want the same app while you try, while you are pregnant and after your baby comes.
picks.price: Google Play Nigeria lists purchases inside the app from ₦4,270 (about $3) to ₦29,000 (about $22).
can: Switch to pregnancy, postpartum or menopause mode.
Read from over 2,000 articles, its listing says.
cannot: Some features are paid purchases inside the app, on both stores.

reviews.title: Why women look elsewhere: what they say about Flo

why: Women reviewing Flo, Clue and Period Calendar often want to see the price before paying. They also mention upgrade pop-ups, losing dates when they change phone and advice that does not fit where they live. Our Nigerian samples are too small to show how common each concern is.

faq.q: Is there a Flo alternative that needs no account?
faq.a: The Wholesome Girlies Period Tracker and Ovulation Calculator open with no sign-in. Period Calendar's App Store listing says you can use it without an account. Flo's Anonymous Mode lets you use Flo without giving your name or email. Clue offers an account at no cost.

faq.q: Which alternative is best for trying to conceive?
faq.a: Choose Wholesome Girlies if you want clinic questions and a partner checklist. Choose Clue for expert-written guides. Choose Period Calendar for reminders and years of saved dates.

faq.q: Do these apps predict ovulation accurately?
faq.a: No app on this page can detect ovulation from dates alone. A Journal of Medical Internet Research analysis of 7,043 tracked cycles found ovulation does not sit reliably at the midpoint. Take your last three or four period dates to a clinician.

doctor: See a doctor after twelve months of trying, or six months if you are over 35. See one sooner if your cycles are very irregular, shorter than 21 days or longer than 35, or have stopped. Take your last three or four period dates with you.

disclaimer.strong: This page compares apps. It cannot tell you when you will conceive.
disclaimer.rest: A calendar predicts and does not detect. It is educational, not medical advice, and no clinician has reviewed it yet.
